scene1_screen2.text: The day’s official work is done, but Christina and her mentor Elisa remain — the last ones in the building. Dust floats in the stale air, settling on towers of unfilled documents.

scene1_screen3.text: Shall we wrap up? It’s past ten already.

scene1_screen4.text: (nervously) I think I´ll stay for a bit longer. I still have so much to sort through, unfortunately.

scene1_screen5.text: In her pocket, a folded envelope weighs heavier than it should. The anonymous note inside was short, almost cryptic: “12A / 1982 — before they erase it for good.”

scene1_screen6.text: Christina had almost thrown it away. But the date… it matched the year her father died in what was called an accident abroad.

scene1_screen7.text: (suspiciously) Just don’t go too deep into the vault. Some doors are better left unopened. See you in the morning.

scene1_screen8.text: Elisa leaves. Christina’s footsteps echo through the narrow aisles. She scans the rows until she finds the marker she’s looking for: Box 12A / 1982.

scene1_screen9.text: Inside the box: an unmarked envelope, singed at the edges, stamped CONFIDENTIAL. A grainy photo slips out — a burning embassy, March 1982. In the foreground, a man mid-stride, his face unmistakable: Andrew Rainer. Attached: a small roll of microfilm.

scene1_screen11.text: The hum of the lights is broken by a voice behind her.

scene1_screen12.text: (sweetly sarcastic) Still chasing ghosts? Some habits don’t die.

scene1_screen13.text: She turns sharply. Leaning against the vault doorframe — Andrew Rainer. The man who vanished years ago without explanation. The man she once trusted more than anyone.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen1.text: You don’t get to walk in here like everything was fine the last time we spoke.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (smirks) What can I say? I missed you too, Chris.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen3.text: Cut the act. If you’re here, it’s bad. Talk.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen4.text: (serious) That file you're holding? You weren’t supposed to find it. You know it, right?

scene1_choice1_option2_screen1.text: (biting) Let me guess: you lost something again. A microfilm? A lie?

scene1_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (with a soft laugh) Just my touch for dramatic entrances, apparently.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen3.text: You think this is a joke? Why is your name here?

scene1_choice1_option2_screen4.text: (steps forward) I think you’re about to dig into something that could get you killed. And I might be the only one who can stop that.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (quietly, cautiously) This... isn´t just about you, is it?

scene1_choice1_option3_screen3.text: Then why did you disappear? Why leave me to chase smoke?

scene1_choice1_option3_screen4.text: (gently) Because if I told you what I knew back then… you'd be dead.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen5.text: (eyes locked on him) Then start talking. Because I’m done running in circles.

scene1_screen14.text: A faint metallic click echoes from deeper in the vault — not the sound of filing cabinets, but of a door unlocking. Christina freezes.

scene1_screen15.text: (low, urgent) That’s not the night guard. They’re here for you. And they won’t knock twice.

scene1_screen18.text: Her gaze shifts to the scorched folder in her hands. If she stays, the file might be gone forever. If she leaves… she’ll be walking straight into Andrew’s shadow again.

scene1_screen20.text: He nods once, taking her elbow. They slip into the darkened corridor, the echo of footsteps closing in behind them.

scene2_screen1.text: They emerge from the archives into the damp London night. Andrew leads Christina through narrow backstreets, keeping to the shadows until they climb a rusted fire escape.

scene2_screen2.text: Above the city’s glittering skyline, Andrew stands with his coat collar turned against the wind. Across the street, shadows move inside the government building — too many for this hour.

scene2_screen3.text: A blinking red light signals a camera tracking them. Someone is watching.

scene2_screen4.text: (approaching) You always did prefer the high ground. Watching from above while the rest of us cleaned up the mess.

scene2_screen5.text: (sweetly sarcastic) I missed your bedtime lectures. You still work late nights, or is this personal?

scene2_screen6.text: Maybe both. But enough of the jokes. Why drag me up here?

scene2_screen7.text: The silence between them is heavier than the wind. Years of unspoken words crackle in the cold air. Below them: the target building tied to the old file. And whatever secret Andrew's not saying.

opts.text: Cover up the tension with protectiveness

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: (grimly) I should’ve burned that file when I had the chance.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (steps closer) But you didn’t. You kept it. Why?

scene2_choice1_option1_screen3.text: (avoiding her eyes) Because I wasn’t sure if I was the villain… or the witness.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen4.text: (quietly) You think I’ll forgive you either way?

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: (calculating) You’re getting too close. You always did have terrible timing.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (flatly) Says the man hiding on rooftops.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: Some people want that file destroyed — and anyone who’s read it.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: Then I guess we’re both already targets.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen5.text: (nods once) Exactly. That’s why I’m here.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (softly) I didn’t expect to see you again. Not like this.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (gaze steady) Then you underestimated me. Again.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (quiet smile) Or maybe I hoped you’d stay out of it. Stay safe. Stay alive.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen4.text: (shaking her head) You don’t get to try to protect me from a distance, Andrew. Not anymore.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen5.text: (serious) Then let me protect you, here and now.

scene2_screen8.text: They stay on the rooftop, watching the movement below. Hours pass in tense observation. Andrew points out patterns — people entering without swiping badges, lights flashing in certain windows.

scene2_screen10.text: Now, we disappear for the night. They’ll already be looking for you.

scene2_screen11.text: He moves quickly, leading her down the fire escape and into the rain-slick streets

scene2_screen12.text: A few blocks away, they reach a run-down motel.

scene2_screen13.text: Inside, they take separate rooms. Christina lies awake, the echo of Andrew’s words chasing her into uneasy dreams.

scene3_screen1.text: Morning comes grey and wet. They meet in a small café down the road, choosing a corner table away from the window.

scene3_screen2.text: Christina wraps her hands around a mug of coffee, holding it like it might keep her grounded. Andrew sips tea, eyes flicking to the door every time it opens.

scene3_screen3.text: You’ve been staring at the street since we sat down.

scene3_screen4.text: Habit. You learn to keep your exits in sight.

scene3_screen5.text: Or maybe you’re afraid I’ll walk out.

scene3_screen6.text: (half-smiles) If you were going to, you’d have done it years ago.

scene3_screen7.text: For a fleeting moment, the tension eases. But it doesn’t last.

scene3_screen8.text: Back at the motel, the door to Christina’s room hangs ajar.

scene3_screen9.text: Her heels crunch on broken glass as she steps inside. The room is a wreck — papers torn, drawers overturned, the safe pried open. The air smells faintly of burnt paper and cologne.

scene3_screen10.text: Either someone’s trying to erase history… or they’re one step ahead of me.

scene3_screen11.text: A glint in the floor vent catches her eye. She reaches in, pulling out a small roll of microfilm — identical to the one from the vault.

scene3_screen12.text: The door closes behind her with a click. Andrew stands there, no shadows left to hide in.

scene3_choice1.text: How do you get the answers?

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: If you came to kill me, just get it over with.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen2.text: If I wanted you dead, I wouldn’t have let you hang on to that film.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen4.text: (earnest) Because if you play this wrong, a lot more people will disappear. Including you.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen1.text: (holding up the microfilm) Start talking. What’s on here?

scene3_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (pauses) The truth about a political murder in ’82 — and who kept it buried.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (crosses her arms) You’re not here to protect me. You’re here to control what I find.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (taking a step forward) I’m here because if you go public with what´s on that microfilm, people will die. Real people. Not just names in a file.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (hard stare) Then we will rewrite the ending. Together.

scene3_screen13.text: Andrew’s gaze shifts to the microfilm in her hand.

scene3_screen14.text: The man who ordered the hit in ’82… and the woman who helped cover it up.

scene3_screen15.text: Christina’s pulse spikes. The air feels heavier.

scene3_screen18.text: The name lands like a blow. Her mentor. The woman who taught her everything.

scene3_screen19.text: (quiet, almost to herself) No… she wouldn’t. Not her.

scene3_screen20.text: But she did. And now you’re holding the proof.

scene3_screen21.text: They lock eyes for a moment — the weight of betrayal between them almost louder than the rain outside.

scene3_screen22.text: From the window, the low rumble of an engine. A dark sedan idles at the far end of the street — two silhouettes inside, unmoving. Andrew follows her gaze.

scene3_screen23.text: They’re not here for a visit. Pack light.

scene3_screen24.text: She doesn’t argue. This time, leaving isn’t about fear — it’s about finding Elisa before someone else finds them.

scene3_screen25.text: Fifteen minutes later, they’re at the station, weaving through the sparse late-night crowd. The smell of wet stone and diesel fills the air.

scene3_screen26.text: Andrew doesn’t slow his pace until they’re at the ticket counter. He slides cash across without a word.

scene3_screen27.text: Where are we going this time?

scene3_screen29.text: She looks at the destination on the ticket — a small rural town hours away from London. To buy some time, and maybe an advantage, before they face Elisa.

scene4_screen1.text: The train hums quietly beneath them. Rain slides down the glass in silver streaks, blurring the world outside into shadows and light.

scene4_screen2.text: Christina sits across from Andrew, the microfilm between them on the small table — a silent weight neither wants to touch.

scene4_screen3.text: You’ve barely said a word since the station.

scene4_screen4.text: (quietly) Sometimes it’s better to think before you speak. Especially when you’re deciding how much truth to give someone.

scene4_screen5.text: (scoffs) And I guess you’ve been rationing mine for years.

scene4_screen6.text: For a long moment, he just watches her, the train’s motion swaying them gently. His gaze is guarded, but not cold — more like someone bracing for impact.

opts.text: Admit you’ve been keeping her away on purpose

scene4_choice1_option1_screen1.text: (softly) There’s something you don’t know about that night in ‘82.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (sarcastically) Let me guess. You were there.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen3.text: (nods) Not just there. I... was how they got the job done.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen5.text: (quietly) I was the reason he died. But not the one who gave the order.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen6.text: (turning to him) And now you expect me to trust you with the truth?

scene4_choice1_option1_screen7.text: (pleading) No. I expect you to decide what to do with it.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen1.text: You think it’s a coincidence we haven’t seen each other in years?

scene4_choice1_option2_screen3.text: I kept my distance because every time you get close to this, someone ends up dead. I didn’t want it to be you.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen5.text: Because you wouldn’t stop looking. You never do.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (sighs) You don’t get it. You were never supposed to find that file.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen2.text: (icy) You keep saying that like I’m the problem.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen3.text: (leaning closer) Because you are. Because you are — the last loose end they didn’t account for. And the only way I know how to protect you is to stay by your side.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen4.text: (whispers) That sounds a lot like you’re scared.

scene4_screen7.text: Christina leans forward, her voice tight.

scene4_screen8.text: And that accident in ’82… the one they buried in reports. My father was there.

scene4_screen9.text: Her voice catches on the word father.

scene4_screen10.text: Tell me it’s not the same night.

scene4_screen12.text: The rhythm of the train seems slower now, the air heavier between them. She leans back, eyes on him, searching for the man she used to know — and wondering if he was ever real.

scene4_screen13.text: A sharp sway of the carriage tilts them closer; his knee brushes hers. Neither moves away.

scene4_screen14.text: (quietly) Whatever happens when we go back for Elisa… we go in together. No lies.

scene4_screen15.text: She exhales slowly, the name still burning in her chest. Every mile the train carries them is a mile further from danger — and closer to the moment they’ll have to decide their next steps.

scene5_screen1.text: They walk for nearly twenty minutes from the station, weaving through quiet rainy streets until Andrew stops in front of a shuttered bookshop.

scene5_screen2.text: Without a word, he unlocks a narrow side door and leads her inside.

scene5_screen3.text: The place smells of dust and paper. Christina scans the cramped room: scuffed floorboards, a kettle gone cold, a stack of blank cassettes. The microfilm in her pocket feels heavier than before, like it can hear them breathe.

scene5_screen4.text: (flatly) So this is where spies hide when they run out of lies?

scene5_screen5.text: (sarcastically) It was either this or a barn.

scene5_screen6.text: The banter fades quickly. The silence between them is full — of what they’ve said, and what they haven’t.

scene5_screen7.text: You’ve known about Elisa for a long time. Haven’t you?

scene5_screen8.text: (nods) I didn’t want you near her once I figured out what she’d done.

scene5_screen9.text: You think you’re protecting me, but you’re just deciding for me.

scene5_screen10.text: He takes a step closer, his voice lower.

scene5_screen11.text: And if I told you your father wasn’t just collateral that night… would you still want the truth?

scene5_screen14.text: He was in that embassy because he was trying to stop the same operation Elisa signed off on. And I was there to make sure it went through.

scene5_screen15.text: The air feels too close now — but neither moves away.

opts.text: Confront, but force a vow with teeth

scene5_choice1_option1_screen1.text: You should have told me from the start.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen4.text: (steadier) I wouldn’t. I thought silence hurt less. I was wrong. I’m on your side now, and I’ll stay there to the end. I won’t make the same mistakes again.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen6.text: (quiet) Ten minutes before the blast. He asked me to pull the alarm. I didn’t. I told myself it wouldn’t change the outcome. That’s the mistake I won’t make again.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen7.text: The vow lands — not as absolution, but as a line he’ll have to prove with every step.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen1.text: She holds his stare a heartbeat too long. The words crowd her throat and break apart.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen2.text: I should hate you for this.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen3.text: I know. And I will understand.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen4.text: But I can’t. Not right now.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen5.text: She steps in. His hesitation lasts a second, then his arms fold around her. The first kiss is cautious, before heat edges in, turning apology into something that tastes like relief and rain.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen7.text: He rests his forehead on hers.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen8.text: She closes her eyes. It isn’t forgiveness. But it is a choice to let him stand close.

scene5_screen16.text: The safehouse settles around them. Outside, the rain softens to a hush. Inside, the table waits: the projector, the coil of truth, the notepad of names.

scene5_screen17.text: Christina sets her bag on the table, pulls the microfilm from her coat pocket. Her fingers hover over the projector’s cold metal frame.

scene5_screen18.text: You sure you want to see it tonight?

scene5_screen19.text: (quiet, firm) I didn’t come here to sleep.

scene5_screen20.text: She threads the film. The machine hums, light spilling onto the wall. Embassy corridors flicker into view.

scene5_screen21.text: “…eliminate him before the leak spreads. He knows too much.”

scene5_screen22.text: “It’s handled. The file will disappear with him.”

scene5_screen23.text: A figure steps into frame — her father — mid-argument with Elisa. His gestures are sharp, urgent, almost desperate. Her chest tightens; the sound is gone now, swallowed by the reel’s mechanical breath.

scene5_screen24.text: The image jumps. A new shot — a close-up of a folder in Elisa’s hands. Its tab reads “Operative Liaison – A. Hale”. She passes it to an unseen third figure, only their gloved hand visible.

scene5_screen27.text: (looking at him sharply) You know the name?

scene5_screen28.text: (grim) Everyone in the old files does. But no one ever lived long enough to prove he exists.

scene5_screen29.text: Then why was Elisa handing him intel?

scene5_screen30.text: Because Hale wasn’t just an operative. He was the contingency. The one they sent when everything else failed.

scene5_screen31.text: The reel clicks to an end, tail flapping in the projector. Christina doesn’t move. Her thoughts race, throat dry.

scene5_screen32.text: (quietly) He’s still out there, isn’t he?

scene5_screen33.text: (tense) If that tape surfaced… he already knows your name.

scene5_screen34.text: She rewinds the reel in silence, eyes on the screen as if it might flash one more clue.

scene5_screen35.text: Tomorrow, we find Elisa. (beat) Because if we want to know who else was in that room — and what they’re planning now — she’s the only one left who can tell us.

scene5_screen36.text: Outside, the rain has stopped — but inside еру safehouse, the storm is just beginning.

scene6_screen1.text: They arrive just after dawn. No sirens. No press. Only the weight of unfinished history.

scene6_screen2.text: Elisa opens the door before they knock. She’s not surprised. Not armed. But not afraid either.

scene6_screen3.text: (calmly) You really should have burned that tape.

scene6_screen4.text: (quiet) You handed him the file. “Operative Liaison – A. Hale.” He’s real.

scene6_screen6.text: Elisa doesn’t blink. Instead, she gestures them in. The apartment is strangely warm, like a trap that pretends to be home.

scene6_screen7.text: So. You’ve seen the last frame. Heard the last names. You came here to… what? Arrest me?

scene6_screen8.text: That depends. How fast can you run?

scene6_screen9.text: She smiles faintly. Then something shatters.

scene6_screen10.text: A window explodes inward. Glass rains over the floor. A shot echoes. Then another. Gunfire. Controlled. Professional. Suppression fire.

scene6_screen12.text: He tackles Christina to the floor as bullets tear through the walls. The bookshelf collapses. The projector sparks, whines, then dies.

scene6_screen13.text: Elisa stays crouched behind a table. Calm. Calculating.

scene6_screen14.text: (low, urgent) That’ll be Hale’s men. He doesn’t miss when he cleans up

scene6_screen15.text: She presses a switch under the floorboard. A section of the wall slides open, revealing a concealed passage behind a bookshelf. A go-bag and two sealed envelopes sit waiting on a ledge.

scene6_screen16.text: (pulls the bag out) I always planned for this day. I just didn’t expect to offer it to you.

scene6_screen17.text: She tosses the envelopes on the floor. Inside — passports, cash, tickets, safehouse coordinates. Everything needed to disappear.

scene6_screen18.text: (staring at the documents) You want me to run?

scene6_screen20.text: (suspicious) You don’t do things out of kindness.

scene6_screen21.text: True. I do them out of necessity. (beat) If you go public now, Hale won’t just erase me. He’ll erase you. You, and everyone who touched that file.

scene6_screen22.text: The gunfire outside pauses — a shift in tactic. They’re moving.

scene6_screen23.text: You have two choices. (looks to Christina) You can take this and disappear. New names, new cities. Or… walk out that door, leak the truth — and start a war you won’t survive.

scene6_screen24.text: Christina’s heart pounds. The truth — her father’s murder, the betrayal, the ghosts — demands justice. But the part of her that’s still human — wants to live.

scene6_screen25.text: (softly) Whatever you choose… I’m with you. Whether we vanish into smoke, or set the whole damn thing on fire — I won’t leave again.

scene6_screen26.text: The folder with Hale’s name still lies on the floor. Bloodstained glass sparkles beside it.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen2.text: She grabs one of the passports, the go-bag, and Andrew’s hand.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen3.text: (quietly) Let’s go before I change my mind.

scene6_choice1_option1_screen4.text: They vanish into the passage. Elisa shuts the wall behind them. A beat later — gunfire floods the room again.

scene7_choice0_option1_screen6.text: They crossed two borders by morning. Burned their names by noon. By nightfall, Christina was gone — at least the version the world knew.

scene7_choice0_option1_screen7.text: Now, she goes by Elise. Works in a used bookstore. Keeps her hair shorter. Sleeps with the curtains closed.

scene7_choice0_option1_screen8.text: Andrew’s presence is steady but silent. He repairs fishing nets. Reads foreign newspapers. Still checks the locks twice at night.

scene7_choice0_option1_screen9.text: No one speaks of Hale. Or Elisa. Or London. Some nights, they pretend it was just a dream — a life someone else lived.

scene7_choice0_option1_screen10.text: (softly) Do you think we made the right choice?

scene7_choice0_option1_screen11.text: (quiet, looking at her) You’re alive. I’m with you. That’s enough for me.

scene7_choice0_option1_screen12.text: A seagull cries outside. The tide rolls in. The world keeps spinning — indifferent.

scene7_choice0_option1_screen13.text: She still dreams of archives. Of flickering reels. Sometimes, she wakes up whispering names no one remembers. And still, when morning comes and he’s beside her — she knows they chose life.

scene7_choice0_option1_screen14.text: They left the truth behind. But it never really stopped following them. Was survival worth the silence? Or just another kind of sentence? Discuss in chat with your partner!

scene7_choice0_option2_screen1.text: I’m done hiding. My father died for the truth. I won’t bury it now.

scene7_choice0_option2_screen2.text: She picks up the folder, slings the go-bag over her shoulder, but leaves the passport behind.

scene7_choice0_option2_screen4.text: (nods) Then we move now. We won’t get a second chance.

scene7_choice0_option2_screen5.text: Elisa watches them go, eyes unreadable.

scene7_choice0_option2_screen6.text: (softly, to herself) You really are your father’s daughter.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen8.text: The footage leaked. The files followed. Names. Faces. Dates. Voices from the past, echoing into the present.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen9.text: For 72 hours, the world didn’t blink.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen10.text: Elisa disappeared before they could reach her. Some say she was never real. Others say Hale got to her first. No one says her name in the open anymore.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen11.text: Christina stood before cameras, steady and unshaking. Not as a whistleblower. Not as a victim. As someone who refused to be quiet.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen12.text: Do you regret what you did?

scene8_choice0_option2_screen13.text: (after a long pause) No. But I regret how long it took.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen14.text: The fallout was immediate. Investigations reopened. Statues came down. A few retired men vanished overnight.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen15.text: She still gets letters. From sons of forgotten diplomats. Daughters of silenced translators. One of them wrote: “Because of you, I found my father’s name again.”

scene8_choice0_option2_screen16.text: They never hid again. She used her name. He stayed in the shadows. Not out of fear — but by choice. Someone had to stay quiet… to keep the noise at bay.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen17.text: Sometimes, when no one’s watching, she slips her hand into his. And he squeezes back — like a promise: You did it. We did it. Together.

scene8_choice0_option2_screen18.text: The world heard her voice. But behind every word — was someone who stayed. Would you reveal the truth? Discuss the story in chat with your partner.
